newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/8, NYC retail starts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/8, NYC retail starts.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were up 1/8 in quiet trade Friday, while Lehman Brothers started a retail order period for New York City's $739 million general obligation bond offering set for next week.

"We are up a solid 1/8," said one trader, who noted the municipal market fared well this week overall. "It is kind of thin, the market has a good tone. Then again, a lot of customers are not around, and we are trading on this atmosphere."
"It was a good week with a fair amount of trading and good two-way flow," he said.
Preliminary estimates of next week's supply total $2.4 billion.

Lehman Brothers started the New York City retail order period, offering the 2016 maturity at a six percent yield. Lehman Brothers is slated to bring a $739 million New York City GO deal on Wednesday. The offering, the week's largest, is one of 29 scheduled negotiated issues totaling $1.5 billion.
Tuesday's $285 million Nevada offering is the largest scheduled competive offering. Seventy-seven competitive issues totaling $924 million are scheduled next week.
One trader said the city deal should do well, noting there is an appetite for New York paper.

While municipals held their own on Friday, the government market continued to lose ground in the wake of the Commerce Department's report that said housing starts for April were up 2.6 percent to a 1.473 million unit annual rate. That was slightly higher-than-expected, as Wall Street economists had forecast starts at a 1.43 million rate.
The long bond was off 11/32 at midday, moving to 96-19/32 and pushing the yield higher to 6.89 percent.

Traders said Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee will keep a lid on activity Friday and Monday, as investors remain sidelined by conflicting views of where short-term rates are headed.
A municipal market participant said the muni market will follow the Treasury market in the wake of any possible Fed action next week.
In debt futures Friday, the June municipal contract was up 4/32 to 116-14/32, while June T-bonds lost 7/32 to 110-3/32. The MOB spread widened to 203 ticks from 192 at the close Thursday.
